additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating an unusually large amount of food in a discrete period with a subjective loss of control, accompanied by features such as eating when not hungry, eating until uncomfortably full, and eating alone because of embarrassment. It typically develops over weeks to months and becomes clinically significant when the pattern is recurrent and distressing, without the compensatory behaviors that would suggest bulimia nervosa.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: When Alejandro’s widowed older cousin from Jalisco moved into the Houston home, his orderly retirement routine shifted into a busier household built around family meals, shared memories, and constant trays of tamales, mole, and pan dulce. Over the next 4 months, he began staying up after everyone went to bed to put away leftovers, and what started as tasting his own cooking became episodes of eating much more than he intended, even when he was not hungry and sometimes until he felt physically uncomfortable. Because he was embarrassed that a careful, self-disciplined man like him could feel unable to stop, he kept these episodes to himself in the garage workshop or while revising his home-maintenance handbook. He mentioned the pattern during a routine primary-care visit after asking whether late-night overeating could be related to retirement stress, and his physician referred him for psychiatric evaluation.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Some nights after supper, when I’m supposed to be putting away the tamales or mole, I’ll end up eating several servings plus pan dulce in the garage, more than I’d ever put on a plate if the family was watching.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What brings me in is that once I start picking at the leftovers late at night, it feels like the sensible part of me is saying, 'That’s enough, Alejandro,' but my hand keeps going back for more anyway.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I don’t usually get sick, but I’ve eaten enough that my belt feels tight and I have to sit in my workshop chair for a while because my stomach is so uncomfortable.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of the time I’m not even hungry, because I already had a good dinner with everyone, but later I still find myself opening containers and tasting one thing after another.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I make sure I do it after the house is quiet or out in the garage because I’d be embarrassed for my cousin or my family to see how much I’m eating when I’m supposed to be the disciplined one.

add_requirements.The binge eating occurs, on average, at: Looking back, these late-night leftover episodes have been happening at least once most weeks, often two nights, since my cousin moved in.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still keeping up with my errands, appointments, and helping around the house, but the mornings after it happens I feel sluggish and less proud of how I’m handling myself.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 4 months, since my older cousin came to live with us.
